easy.def: A room where scientists work.
examples: The scientist is in the lab.
We visited a lab.
The lab has tools.

more.def: A room or building where scientists do experiments.
examples: The scientist mixed chemicals in the lab.
Our class visited a science lab.
The lab has microscopes and tubes.

easy.def: Not having enough of something.
examples: A lack of rain hurt the plants.
The lack of light made it hard to read.
A lack of sleep made him tired.

more.def: A condition of not having enough of something.
examples: A lack of rain made the garden dry.
The lack of snow meant we could not go sledding.
A lack of sleep makes it hard to learn.

easy.def: To not have enough of something.
examples: The plants lack water.
The soup lacks salt.
We lack a goalie.

more.def: To be without something, or not to have enough of it.
examples: The broth lacks flavor.
Our team lacks a good goalie this year.
Some desert plants lack leaves and have spines instead.

easy.def: A boy.
examples: The lad ran home.
A young lad helped us.
The lads played ball.

more.def: A boy or young man.
examples: The lad carried the basket to the market.
A young lad sold newspapers on the corner.
The lads in the story went fishing.

easy.def: A polite word for a woman.
examples: The lady smiled.
A kind lady helped me.
That lady has a hat.

more.def: A polite word for a woman, especially a grown-up.
examples: The lady at the bakery gave us each a free cookie.
An old lady held the door for the children.
Ladies and gentlemen, the show is about to begin.

easy.def: A big body of water with land around it.
examples: We swim in the lake.
The lake is blue.
Ducks live on the lake.

more.def: A large body of fresh water with land all around it.
examples: We swam in the cool lake.
Ducks paddled across the lake.
The lake froze over in winter.

easy.def: The dry part of the Earth.
examples: The ship reached land.
Frogs live on land and in water.
The land is flat here.

more.def: The solid part of the Earth's surface that is not covered by water.
examples: After days at sea, the sailors saw land.
Farmers plant crops on good land.
Turtles lay their eggs on land.

easy.def: To come down from the air.
examples: The plane will land.
The bird landed.
A bee landed on my hand.

more.def: To come down to the ground or water after flying.
examples: The plane landed safely at the airport.
A butterfly landed on my finger.
The geese landed on the lake.

easy.def: A narrow road.
examples: We walked down the lane.
A country lane.
The lane is quiet.

more.def: A narrow road or path.
examples: We walked down a quiet country lane.
A dirt lane led to the farm.
The lane was lined with trees.

easy.def: A strip for one line of cars or swimmers.
examples: Stay in your lane.
The pool has six lanes.
The road has two lanes.

more.def: A strip of road, track or pool for one line of cars, runners or swimmers.
examples: Stay in your lane when you swim.
The highway has three lanes.
Each runner had a lane on the track.

easy.def: The words people use to talk and write.
examples: Spanish is a language.
Babies learn language by listening.
Sign language uses your hands.

more.def: A system of words that people use to speak, write, and understand each other.
examples: She can speak three languages: English, French, and Arabic.
People who cannot hear may use sign language.
He is learning a new language before his trip.

easy.def: Big.
examples: A large dog.
The box is large.
A large cup of milk.

more.def: Big in size or amount.
examples: A large crowd gathered in the park.
The elephant is the largest land animal.
She ordered a large glass of milk.

easy.def: Coming after all the others.
examples: I was last in line.
This is the last page.
She ate the last grape.

more.def: Coming at the end, or most recent.
examples: The last bus leaves the station at midnight.
I saw my cousins last summer.
He ate the last slice of pizza on the plate.

easy.def: To go on for a time.
examples: The show lasts one hour.
The snow did not last.
Will the toy last?

more.def: To continue for a certain length of time, or to stay in good condition.
examples: The storm lasted all night, but the morning was calm.
These strong boots will last for years.
A summer day lasts longer than a winter day.

easy.def: After the right time.
examples: I am late.
The bus is late.
It is late at night.

more.def: Coming after the expected time, or near the end of a period of time.
examples: The train was late because of the snow.
We stayed up late on New Year's Eve.
The leaves fall in late autumn.

easy.def: After the right time.
examples: She woke up late.
We ate late.
He got to school late.

more.def: After the usual or expected time.
examples: I woke up late, so I missed the bus.
The movie ended late, and we got home after dark.
She arrived late and tiptoed to her seat.

easy.def: After this time.
examples: See you later.
I will eat later.
She came later.

more.def: At a time after now, or after another time that was named.
examples: I will do my homework later, after we play outside.
The rain stopped, and the sun came out an hour later.
We can talk about it later.

easy.def: To make happy sounds because something is funny.
examples: I laugh at funny jokes.
The baby laughed.
We laughed at the clown.

more.def: To make sounds with your voice that show you think something is funny or you are happy.
examples: The whole class laughed at the silly story.
She laughed so hard that her stomach hurt.
Dad laughs whenever the dog chases its tail.

easy.def: The sound you make when something is funny.
examples: She has a loud laugh.
We had a good laugh.
I heard his laugh in the next room.

more.def: The happy sound a person makes when something is funny.
examples: Her laugh is so loud that you can hear it across the playground.
The joke got a big laugh from everyone.
We had a good laugh about the mix-up.

easy.def: The sound of people laughing.
examples: I heard laughter from the playground.
The joke filled the room with laughter.
Laughter is a happy sound.

more.def: The sound or act of laughing.
examples: The room filled with laughter when the clown came in.
Their laughter could be heard down the hall.
The funny movie brought tears of laughter.

easy.def: To send something up or out into the air or water.
examples: They will launch the rocket.
We launched a boat.
He launched the kite.

more.def: To send something such as a rocket or boat out with force, or to start something new.
examples: The scientists launched a rocket into space.
The crew launched the boat from the shore.
The school will launch a new reading club this fall.

easy.def: The sending of a rocket or boat.
examples: We watched the launch on TV.
The launch was loud.
The boat launch was fun.

more.def: The act of sending a rocket, ship or something new out into the world.
examples: The whole class watched the launch of the space shuttle.
A boat launch let us slide our canoe into the water.
The launch of the new book was a big event.

easy.def: A rule that everyone in a place must follow.
examples: It is a law to wear a seat belt.
The town made a new law.
Every country has laws.

more.def: A rule made by the government that people must obey.
examples: There is a law that cars must stop for school buses.
The mayor signed a new law about recycling.
Laws help keep people safe.

easy.def: A person with a job helping people with the law.
examples: The lawyer works in court.
My aunt is a lawyer.
A lawyer reads many laws.

more.def: A person whose job is to give advice about laws and speak for people in court.
examples: My aunt is a lawyer who helps families.
The lawyer spoke to the judge.
Lawyers study the law for many years.

easy.def: To put something down gently.
examples: Lay the book on the table.
Mom laid the baby in the crib.
Lay your coat here.

more.def: To put something down in a flat or careful way.
examples: Lay the cards face down on the table.
She laid the baby in the crib.
Workers laid bricks in a neat row.

easy.def: To make an egg.
examples: Hens lay eggs.
The hen laid an egg.
Birds lay eggs in nests.

more.def: To produce an egg from the body.
examples: Chickens lay eggs almost every day.
The turtle crawled up the beach to lay her eggs.
Robins lay blue eggs in the spring.

easy.def: Not wanting to work or move.
examples: The lazy cat slept all day.
I feel lazy on hot days.
A lazy dog lay in the sun.

more.def: Not willing to work or use energy.
examples: He felt too lazy to get up and close the door.
We spent a lazy afternoon reading by the pool.
He was too lazy to put his dishes in the sink.
